SUMED is a crude oil transshipment pipeline; both sources describe it as such.
Actively operating and carrying record/near-record throughput as of 2026 per current Egyptian press coverage; EIA background confirms the standing 2.5M bpd design capacity.

Operator's own history page: 'SUMED was established by Law No 7, 1974' (January 1974). resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: SUMED (Suez-Mediterranean Pipeline) is one of the best-documented crude oil pipelines in the world — a strategic Suez Canal bypass built after the 1967 canal closure. Confirmed independently by: Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumed_pipeline), the operator's own site (sumed.org), the U.S. EIA (eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=61025), and current 2026 reporting (Egypt Independent, 'Egypt's SUMED oil flows jump 150% on Red Sea trade rerouting') confirming it is actively operating today amid Red Sea shipping disruptions. Correctly classified Fuel=Oil (crude oil transshipment line, not gas/products). No hallucination risk here — this is a Tier-1 real, active, well-known asset.

resolutions.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE WATCHLIST RESOLVED: P0530 and P5121 both read 'Sumed Oil Pipeline', Ain Sukhna->Alexandria, 320 km / 42 in / 1,250,000 bpd — identical on every visible spec. This is NOT a duplicate/relabel. Multiple independent sources (Wikipedia, sumed.org's own facilities page) confirm SUMED is physically built as TWO PARALLEL 42-inch, 320 km pipelines sharing one corridor (Ain Sukhna -> Dahshour booster -> Sidi Kerir), with a combined system capacity of 2.5 million bpd. GEM has deliberately modeled this as two rows via segment_name — P0530 = 'Pipeline 1', P5121 = 'Pipeline 2' — which is the correct way to represent a genuine twin-line system, not a double-count. Minor cross-row inconsistency worth a separate note (not this row's defect): sumed.org's own history page dates the FIRST line's start to January 1977 (first tanker loaded at Sidi Kerir) and the SECOND line/phase to October 1978 (capacity doubled to 80 million tons/yr) — P0530's StartYear1=1977 matches 'Pipeline 1' correctly, but P5121 ('Pipeline 2') also carries StartYear1=1977 in the worklist, which per sumed.org's own timeline should likely be 1978. That is P5121's issue to flag/fix, not this row's.

resolutions.researcher_notes: GEOGRAPHY ERROR: sheet has StartLocation='Ain Sukhna terminal', StartPrefecture/District='Sinai Peninsula', StartState/Province='North Red Sea'. Ain Sukhna (Ain Sokhna) is on the WESTERN/African shore of the Gulf of Suez, in Suez Governorate — roughly 55 km south of Suez city and ~120 km east of Cairo. It is NOT part of the Sinai Peninsula, which lies on the opposite (eastern) side of the Suez Canal/Gulf of Suez. Confirmed via multiple independent sources describing Ain Sokhna as a town in Suez Governorate on the Gulf of Suez's west bank. This is also an internal-consistency defect: four OTHER Egypt-oil rows in this same tracker that reference the identical Ain Sokhna location (P7331 EndPrefecture/District, P7315 EndPrefecture/District, P7327 StartPrefecture/District, P7321 StartLocation) all correctly write 'Ain Sokhna' — only P0530 and its twin P5121 substitute the wrong 'Sinai Peninsula'. resolutions.recommendation: correct FuelSource from 'Gulf of Suez' to reflect the crude's actual origin — e.g. 'Saudi Arabia (Persian Gulf crude, via Ain Sukhna terminal)' — matching the sheet's own convention of naming a specific origin field/terminal (cf. resolutions.researcher_notes: LIKELY MISATTRIBUTION: FuelSource='Gulf of Suez' appears to conflate the GEOGRAPHIC LOCATION of the intake terminal (Ain Sukhna sits on the Gulf of Suez) with the ACTUAL SOURCE of the crude oil moving through the line. Per gem_schema.md's own convention (documented for the gas sheet but applied identically across every other Egypt-oil FuelSource cell in this worklist), FuelSource should name the specific upstream field/terminal feeding the line, not a generic body of water. SUMED carries NO locally-produced Gulf-of-Suez crude at all — it is a pure transshipment line: VLCCs deliver imported crude to Ain Sukhna, which is then pumped to Sidi Kerir for reloading onto tankers bound for the Mediterranean/Europe. Al Jazeera (2020, still describing the same unchanged system): 'The vast majority of crude entering the pipeline comes from Saudi Arabia, with Kuwait and Iraq contributing much less' and 'designed to pump 2.5 million barrels of Persian Gulf crude'. Wikipedia independently corroborates: SUMED provides 'an alternative to the Suez Canal for transporting oil from the Persian Gulf region to the Mediterranean.' Two independent sources agree the origin is Persian/Arabian Gulf crude (predominantly Saudi), not Gulf-of-Suez production — the current value is not merely imprecise, it names the wrong body of water for the wrong reason (intake geography vs. crude origin).

Status=operating confirmed current as of 2026 (Egypt Independent: 'SUMED oil flows jump 150% on Red Sea trade rerouting', describing live 2026 throughput). ProposalYear=1974 matches sumed.org's own history: 'SUMED was established by Law No 7, 1974' (precursor five-nation agreement was Dec 1973 per a 1973 NYT piece in the wiki's own citation list, so 1974 = formal legal establishment, a defensible ProposalYear anchor). StartYear1=1977 matches sumed.org's own timeline precisely for THIS line ('Pipeline 1'): first tanker (Esthel) loaded at Sidi Kerir January 1977. CAVEAT on Capacity=1,250,000 bpd: no source states a per-line figure explicitly — every source (Wikipedia, EIA, Al Jazeera) states only the combined SYSTEM capacity of 2.5 million bpd across both twin lines. 1,250,000 x 2 = 2,500,000 is an exact, arithmetically consistent split for two identically-specced (42in/320km) parallel lines, but it is a derived value, not a directly cited one — tier medium for Capacity specifically, high for everything else in this cluster.

ORIGINAL FINDING: EXISTENCE + core specs confirmed by 3 independent sources that all name this specific pipeline (not GEM-derived): (1) English Wikipedia 'Sumed pipeline' infobox/body: From Ain Sokhna terminal, To Sidi Kerir port, Length 320 km, Commissioned 1977, two parallel 42-inch lines, aggregate capacity 2.5 million bpd; (2) Al Jazeera/Bloomberg (27 Jul 2020), a live news account of real tanker-tracked flows through the pipeline in 2020, confirming it is an operating asset carrying Persian Gulf crude from Ain Sukhna to Sidi Kerir at up to 2.5 million bpd design capacity; (3) UN ESCWA's terminology database (archive.unescwa.org) independently names 'SUMED' / 'الشركة العربية لأنابيب البترول (سوميد)' as the Arab Petroleum Pipelines Company, a joint venture of EGPC, the Saudi oil company, three Kuwaiti companies and Qatar Petroleum -- an EXACT match, character for character, to GEM's own Operator string on this row ('الشركة العربية لأنابيب البترول "سوميد"'). GEM's per-line values (Length 320 km, Diameter 42 in, Capacity 1,250,000 bpd, StartYear1 1977, Status operating, Fuel Oil) all check out against these sources for a single line of the twin system.

REVISION (2026-08-27, batch QC): StartYear1 is CARVED OUT of the 'all corroborate' list above. Every source behind that 1977 -- English Wikipedia's infobox 'Commissioned 1977', and ar.wikipedia's category 'بنية تحتية للطاقة اكتملت في 1977' (energy infrastructure completed in 1977) -- dates the SUMED SYSTEM, i.e. the first line. It is an aggregate figure restated on a segment row, the same pattern this project has flagged elsewhere. sumed.org's own history page (traced in P0530's duplicate record in this same batch) dates Pipeline 1 to January 1977 (first tanker, the Esthel, loaded at Sidi Kerir) and Pipeline 2 / the capacity doubling to 80 Mt/y to October 1978. P5121 IS Pipeline 2. See the new concern/spec record below. Everything else in the original finding stands.

resolutions.recommendation: Change StartPrefecture/District from 'Sinai Peninsula' to 'Suez Governorate' (or similar mainland label); also reconcile StartState/Province, which is inconsistent between the two twin rows ('Suez Gulf' here vs 'North Red Sea' on P0530).
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEOGRAPHY ERROR, carried on BOTH twin rows (not unique to P5121 -- checked P0530, same defect). Ain Sukhna (the pipeline's start terminal) is on the WEST shore of the Gulf of Suez, in Suez Governorate, mainland Egypt -- English Wikipedia's 'Ain Sokhna' article infobox gives Governorate = Suez, coordinates 29.6N 32.3167E. The Sinai Peninsula lies on the EAST side of the Gulf of Suez / Suez Canal; Ain Sukhna is not part of it and no source calls it Sinai. GEM's 'StartPrefecture/District: Sinai Peninsula' on P5121 (and P0530) is geographically wrong. Separately, the two twin rows also disagree with each other on 'StartState/Province' ('Suez Gulf' on P5121 vs 'North Red Sea' on P0530) for what should be the identical physical terminal -- an internal inconsistency worth reconciling at the same time. Not staging a replacement value/ref pair here per the no-orphan-cell rule and because correcting a wrong cluster value is an Update-leg edit, not a ref-only fill.

resolutions.recommendation: Change FuelSource from 'Gulf of Suez' to a Persian/Arabian Gulf (Middle East) crude label -- SUMED does not carry Gulf-of-Suez-produced crude, it carries Persian Gulf crude landed by VLCC at Ain Sukhna.
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's FuelSource = 'Gulf of Suez' appears to conflate the pipeline's START LOCATION's geographic feature (the terminal sits on the Gulf of Suez) with the actual origin of the oil it carries, which is a different body of water entirely. Both independent sources that describe the pipeline's purpose are explicit that the crude comes from the Persian/Arabian Gulf, not from Egypt's own (much smaller) Gulf of Suez oil fields: English Wikipedia -- 'It provides an alternative to the Suez Canal for transporting oil from the Persian Gulf region to the Mediterranean'; Al Jazeera/Bloomberg (2020) -- 'the Sumed transports Middle Eastern oil to the North African coast' and 'Egypt's Sumed pipeline was designed to pump 2.5 million barrels of Persian Gulf crude from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean every day.' SUMED exists precisely because VLCCs too large for the Suez Canal offload Persian Gulf crude at Ain Sukhna, which the pipeline then carries to the Mediterranean for reloading -- the fuel source is Persian Gulf crude, not locally produced Gulf of Suez crude. Same defect on P0530 (checked). Not staging a replacement value/ref here (wrong-value correction is an Update-leg edit, not a ref-only fill).

resolutions.pipeline_name: West Esh El-Mallaha-Gebel Az Zeit Oil Pipeline

Every core GEM value matches this single primary trade-press source exactly: Fuel=Oil, LengthKnown=100 km, Capacity=24,000 bpd, Cost=$8,000,000 (article states '$8 million', a prose/unit equivalence -- the existing Cost [ref] on this same OGJ URL was flagged by the automated checker as 'value not found' only because it looked for the digit string '8,000,000' and missed the prose form; the ref IS valid and should NOT be treated as unsupported), StartYear1=2004, Operator=Lukoil Overseas Holding Ltd, FuelSource=West Esh El-Mallaha, EndLocation=Ras El Bikhar terminal, EndPrefecture/District=Gebel Az Zeit. Classification (crude oil field-to-terminal export line) is correct -- this is not a products/LPG line and does not belong in GGIT. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster -- no other row shares this name, these endpoints, or this field (WEEM/West Esh El-Mallaha is unique to this row); not a relabel or segment double-count of any other PID. CAVEAT (why not 'high'): only ONE independent source could be verified this session. The gem.wiki page's second citation, Rigzone 'Lukoil Hits 2 Million Ton Mark at WEEM Field...', is BLOCKED, not deleted -- it returns HTTP 403 directly and via url_verifier (TooManyRedirects/anti-bot behavior on this old article URL), and has zero Wayback Machine snapshots (CDX query empty, /wayback/available returns an empty archived_snapshots object) -- so it could not be read or cited, and per standing rules this is not treated as evidence against the pipeline. WebSearch quota was exhausted this session (200/200) before a second independent source could be located, so tier is capped at medium pending a future search for corroboration (e.g. Lukoil Overseas annual reports, EGPC yearbooks, or a re-fetch of the Rigzone URL). SECONDARY CAVEAT (attribution, low severity): GEM's StartLocation value is 'Easern desert' (also misspelled) -- a vague regional descriptor. The OGJ source is explicit that the pipeline's origin point is 'Khurghada' (Hurghada), which is consistent with StartPrefecture/District='Hurgada' already on the row but more specific than the StartLocation value itself. Recommend correcting StartLocation to 'Hurghada' (or 'Khurghada') to match the sourced route description and fixing the 'Easern'->'Eastern' typo; not staging a ref for the current StartLocation value since the source does not literally support 'Eastern desert' as the specific origin name. resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via an independent, highly authoritative primary source not previously cited on this row: the Egyptian Presidency's own official website (presidency.eg), filed under 'Presidential Openings and National Projects / Petroleum and Natural Gas', title 'Establishment of the Southwest Mleiha oil pipeline in the Western Desert.' Its body text: 'Establishing a pipeline to transport quantities of oil produced from the southwest Mleiha fields to the oil treatment station in the Mleiha area, estimated at about 7 thousand barrels/day, at a cost of 31 million dollars.' This matches GEM's Capacity (7,000 bpd), Cost ($31,000,000), StartLocation (Southwest Mleiha), and EndLocation (Mleiha) EXACTLY, and confirms Fuel=Oil. This is real infrastructure, not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as an oil pipeline; nothing suggests it is gas, NGL, or a non-pipeline facility. DUPLICATE CHECK (roster watchlist item 'P0572 Mleiha-El Hamra vs P5125 Southwest Mleiha - same trunk?'): NOT a duplicate. P0572 (Mleiha oilfield -> Matruh, 167 km, 16in, 140,000 bpd) and P5125 (Southwest Mleiha -> Mleiha, 130 km, 10in, 7,000 bpd) differ sharply in diameter and capacity (20x), and the presidency.eg source itself describes P5125's function as gathering oil FROM the Southwest Mleiha field INTO the Mleiha treatment station -- i.e. P5125 is a feeder line terminating exactly where P0572's larger outbound trunk begins. These are sequential segments of one evacuation system serving different traffic volumes, not a double-counted single pipeline. CAVEAT: the 10-inch diameter is larger than typical for a 7,000 bpd nameflow (~4-6in would be more usual); this is plausible if the line was sized for planned production growth -- a harvested (but 403-blocked, unverifiable) alwafd.news headline title from the wiki citation list ('"Agiba" raises Southwest Mleiha field production to exceed 9,500 barrels of oil per day') suggests field output has grown past the pipeline's original 7,000 bpd rating, consistent with deliberate oversizing. Not flagged as a hard concern since no source contradicts the diameter itself -- left UNRESOLVED (see fills) rather than guessed at.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Read the sheet's own sole cited source (almasryalyoum.com/news/details/3294097, 29-Oct-2024, verified live+content-present) in full. It is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT about this pipeline's identity: the headline and a closing editorial note both call it 'خط منتجات مسطرد- بنها' (Musturad-Banha products line, diameter 16in / length 45km — matching GEM's Diameter/LengthKnown exactly), but the article's own body text describes the actual project as 'مشروع إحلال وتجديد خط المازوت المغذي لشبكة كهرباء مسطرد' (a project to REPLACE/RENEW the mazut line feeding Musturad's power network) whose purpose is 'رفع كفاءة وتأمين نقل المازوت لتغذية محطة كهرباء شبرا الخيمة' (raising efficiency of mazut transport to feed SHUBRA EL-KHEIMA power station) and which 'لم يتم تجديده منذ عام 1984' (has not been renewed since 1984) -- i.e. an aging line feeding a DIFFERENT named destination than Banha. Cross-checked against the Petroleum Pipelines Company's own official FY2023-2024 AGM report, republished near-verbatim by TWO outlets (almasdar.com/146948, verified live; and youm7.com/story/2024/10/10/.../6735756, verified live -- these two are the SAME wire/press-release text, not independent of each other per rule 4). That official company list itemises Egypt's pipeline projects and treats these as TWO SEPARATE, DIFFERENTLY-NAMED items: (1) under 'إحلال وتجديد' (replacement/renewal of existing assets) it lists 'خط مازوت مسطرد / محطة كهرباء شبرا الخيمة' (the Musturad/Shubra El-Kheima mazut line) -- never called 'Banha' anywhere in this text; and (2) under 'رفع الكفاءة' (efficiency-raising/new capacity) it separately lists 'إنشاء خط من مسطرد حتى بنها بطول 52 كم لرفع معدلات تدفيع المنتجات البترولية من منطقة الدلتا إلى مسطرد ومنها إلى السويس' (construction of a NEW 52km Musturad-to-Banha line to boost Delta-to-Suez product throughput) -- this matches P7319 (52km, construction) exactly, both name and length.
